meta.description: One portal for every tool, protocol, and official resource in EPICS, TANGO, and the broader scientific control systems ecosystem.

resources.description: High-performance EPICS archiving service designed for large-scale deployments. Stores Process Variable history in a distributed, scalable backend.
Historical Data Base for TANGO — stores attribute values over time in MySQL, MariaDB, Cassandra or TimescaleDB backends.

Modern successor to Control System Studio (CS-Studio). The standard graphical client for EPICS-based control rooms worldwide. Supports OPI displays, alarms, archiving, and — via the TANGO plugin — TANGO device browsing.
resources.kic_note: Katy Saintin contributed PR #3602 — the TANGO plugin for Phoebus, tested at SOLEIL in 2025.

resources.description: High-level Python framework for TANGO-based GUI applications. Part of the Sardana ecosystem developed at ALBA.

OPC Unified Architecture — the industrial standard for secure, platform-independent communication between PLCs and supervision systems. The EPICS OPC-UA driver by Ralph Lange is used on ITER, PIP-II Fermilab, and CEA/IRFU projects.

The original EPICS networking protocol, designed by Jeff Hill at LANL in the late 1980s. A publish-subscribe 'software bus' connecting EPICS clients and IOCs. Still running on production systems 35 years after its creation.
Next-generation EPICS networking protocol introduced in EPICS 7. Supports structured data types, replacing Channel Access for new deployments while running alongside it.

The official TANGO device server code generator. Created by Pascal Verdier at ESRF. Generates C++, Java, and Python device class skeleton code from a graphical interface, dramatically reducing the effort to create new device servers.
TANGO control system administration tool. Created by Pascal Verdier at ESRF. Monitors and controls Starter device servers across the network.
TANGO database browser and configuration tool. Allows browsing, editing and configuring all device properties in the TANGO database. Essential for any TANGO installation.
The core of the EPICS toolkit — IOC runtime, Channel Access, pvAccess, database record support, and device drivers. The foundation everything else is built on.
The TANGO Controls framework — Device Server runtime, CORBA/ZMQ middleware, database, and client libraries. The foundation of the TANGO ecosystem.
International Conference on Accelerator and Large Experimental Physics Control Systems. The main gathering of the global control systems community, held every two years.
New Opportunities for Better User Group Software — conference focused on data acquisition and analysis software for neutron and synchrotron facilities.
